property_summary: For any user, the sum of their balance and the contract's timestamp must be greater than or equal to the current block timestamp after a successful Put call; the mutant violates this by overwriting the balance, potentially preventing future Collect calls.
After two consecutive Put calls by the same sender with different msg.values, the final balance must equal the sum of both msg.values; the mutant violates this by keeping only the last msg.value.

After any number of Put calls by the same sender, the caller's balance in Acc must be at least the sum of all msg.value sent in those calls; the mutant violates this by always setting the balance to the last msg.value.
For any sender, after two Put calls with different values v1 and v2, Acc.balance is at least the maximum of v1 and v2; the mutant overwrites balance to only the latest msg.value.
After any sequence of Put calls by a sender, the balance in Acc must be at least the sum of all msg.values sent; the mutant violates this by setting balance to only the last msg.value.

After any call to Put, the recorded unlockTime must be at least block.timestamp and also at least the caller-supplied _unlockTime; the bug breaks this by ignoring the user-supplied unlock time and always setting it exactly to block.timestamp.

After a Put, the ability to call Collect without revert depends on the recorded unlockTime versus block.timestamp: the reference lets a future unlockTime block early Collect, the bug always sets unlockTime to block.timestamp, allowing immediate Collect when it should be blocked.

After a Put with a user-supplied unlockTime greater than block.timestamp, the recorded unlockTime in Acc must equal that user-supplied unlockTime, not block.timestamp; the bug always sets it to block.timestamp.

After a Put with _unlockTime > block.timestamp, Acc[caller].unlockTime must be at least _unlockTime, which the reference satisfies; the bug forces it to block.timestamp, making it strictly smaller when _unlockTime > block.timestamp.

After any admissible Put, the recorded unlockTime must equal the user-supplied _unlockTime when _unlockTime >= block.timestamp; the bug always sets unlockTime to block.timestamp regardless of the supplied value.

After any number of calls to Put by any user, the sum of all Acc balances must equal the contract's Ether balance minus any collected amounts; the mutant with subtraction breaks this invariant because Put decreases both the user's balance and the contract's balance, creating a mismatch.
After a user calls Put, their Acc balance must equal the sum of their own msg.value contributions; the mutant subtracting msg.value breaks this because the balance becomes less than total deposits.

After any sequence of calls to Put, the sum of all Acc balances must equal the contract's Ether balance minus any Ether already collected; the mutant with subtraction breaks this invariant because Put reduces both the account balance and the contract balance, while the reference adds to the account balance and the contract, keeping them in sync.
After a call to Put, the caller's Acc balance must be at least the msg.value sent in that call; the bug subtracts msg.value, making the balance smaller than the sent amount.
After a Put, the sum of all Acc balances equals the contract's balance; the mutant subtraction decreases the acc balance but not the contract balance (since ETH is received), breaking the equality.

The sum of all account balances reported by Acc getter must never exceed address(c).balance; the buggy contract allows an overflow in Put to increase the balance while adding less ether, violating this invariant.

After any sequence of Put calls, the sum of all account balances reported by Acc getter must never exceed address(c).balance; the buggy contract allows an overflow in Put to increase the balance while adding less ether, violating this invariant.

After any Put call, the balance of the caller in Acc must be strictly greater than the balance before the call, unless an overflow occurs; the buggy version allows an overflow from an arbitrarily large msg.value combined with a nearly max uint256 balance, causing the post-balance to be less than or equal to the pre-balance, violating the invariant that balance strictly increases on non-zero msg.value.
After a Put call with msg.value > 0, the caller's Acc balance must strictly increase; the buggy version allows an overflow that makes the post-balance ≤ pre-balance.

For any Put call, if the caller's pre-balance plus msg.value does not overflow uint256, then the post-balance must equal the pre-balance plus msg.value; the buggy version removes the overflow check, allowing a non-overflowing Put to leave the balance arbitrarily corrupted by a prior overflow, so the post-balance may not match the arithmetic sum.
After a successful Collect, the contract's balance must decrease by the collected amount.
After a successful Collect, the contract's balance must decrease by the collected amount.
After a successful Collect, the contract's balance must decrease by the collected amount.
After a successful Collect, the contract's balance must decrease by the collected amount.
After a successful Collect, the contract's balance must decrease by the collected amount.

After any Collect call that satisfies the if-condition, the contract's total balance (address(c).balance) must decrease exactly by the collected amount; the buggy mutant leaves the internal balance unchanged but still transfers ether, so the contract loses ether without correctly updating its accounting, possibly allowing more ether to be drained than intended.
After any Collect call that satisfies the if-condition, the caller's Acc balance must decrease by exactly the collected amount _am; the buggy mutant leaves the balance unchanged.

After any Collect call, the sum of all Acc balances plus address(c).balance remains constant for the reference but increases for the buggy version because the balance is not reduced while ether is sent out.

For any caller that successfully executes Collect, the decrease in the caller's Acc balance must equal the ether sent; the buggy version never reduces the Acc balance, so the invariant that the logged Collect amount plus the remaining Acc balance equals the pre-call balance is broken.
Collect should revert when the caller's unlock time has not been reached, regardless of balance
Collect must revert when the caller's balance is below MinSum, regardless of the _am argument.
Calling Collect must revert for any input.
Calling Collect must always revert.
Collect must revert for any input when msg.sender's unlocked balance is below MinSum.

property_summary: For any account with a deposit, the rule is that after a call to Collect, the contract's ETH balance never decreases below MinSum, but the buggy version allows draining the contract below MinSum.
For any account with a nonzero balance, calling Collect should never succeed for an amount greater than the account's balance, but the mutant allows over-withdrawal causing an underflow revert.
For any caller, after a Collect, either the call reverts or the caller's balance decreases by exactly the requested amount; the mutant can succeed without decreasing balance.
For any caller, if Collect reverts then the caller's balance must be unchanged; the mutant can make Collect succeed without decreasing balance, violating this invariant.

After a call to Collect(uint256 _am), if the call succeeds, the caller's Acc balance must decrease by exactly _am (provided the caller's balance was at least _am pre-call), but the mutant allows success without decreasing balance.
A Collect call that does not revert must have been preceded by enough balance and unlocked time, which M violates by allowing Collect even when locked or underfunded.
A Collect call after a Put must revert if the sender's balance or unlock time does not meet requirements.
After calling Put, any attempt to call Collect must revert.
A call to Collect must revert when invoked after Put by the same sender under the given input parameters.
A Collect call must revert after a Put if the sender's balance or unlock time does not meet requirements.
